findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw beef to be stored under eggs in cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage order and beef was moved to above eggs. Ensure proper storage order is maintained to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizing solution to be set up upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was set up and tested at 100 ppm (CL). Ensure sanitizer solution is set up at all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the baffles of the hood system to be heavily soiled with grease and debris. The interior of the fryer and the interior fryer door is soiled with grease. Stove top is heavily soiled with food splash, grease, and debris. Area could use a deep cleaning. Per PIC/owner, hood system is professionally cleaned 1x yearly. Facility fries a considerable amount of food. Hood system could likely use a 2x yearly schedule for professional hood cleaning. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) 1) The prep cooler holding multiple items is observed with internal food temperatures of 49.7 degrees. The only TCS items in the cooler are sliced onions that will be used or discarded within 6 hours (4:30 pm 8/29). 2) The reach in cooler in the facility is observed at approximately 50 degrees. Foods are probed at 37 top 50 degrees. Foods below 41 are being wrapped and placed in the chest freezer in the facility. Foods above cold holding limits (chicken/ bacon/ ground beef) from the day before are discarded during the inspection. TCS foods placed in the cooler this morning (10:30) and above cold holding limits will be used of discarded by 4:30 pm. Follow up on coolers.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15  (C) On arrival, the front and rear doors of the facility are propped open to facilitate ventilation of the facility. Multiple flies are observed in the kitchen area. The doors were closed during the inspection. Inspector will spot check for flies when he returns for the cooler follow up.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540. 

No certified food manager was observed during the inspection. The Sangamon County schedule and application was distributed during the inspection. Any ANSI accredited course will meet the requirements of the code.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Observed American cheese slices without a date marking. Also, a quart size milk is observed in the cooler without a date marking. Date mark and use within 7 Days. Discussed cheeses and the Seven Day Rule. Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d) Observed a carton of eggs being stored over juices. Eggs stored on bottom shelf during inspection.  All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floor drain under the three compartment sink was soiled. Clean the floor drain under the sink.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the bar three compartment sink and the kitchen three compartment sink when the water is turned on. Repair the leaks.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed cheese sauce at 130 F (infrared and bi-metallic metal stem thermometer).  Cheese sauce was made 45 minutes before and is heated on the stove top.  Cheese was brought back up to 165 F and will continue to be hot held at 135 F. Facility can hot hold items at 135 at all times or discard after four hours.  Inspector recommends to use half a can of cheese sauce for lunch and heat the rest of the can for dinner.  Heat cheese sauce as needed.  Cheese is always discarded at the end of the day and a new can is used for lunch everyday.
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the fan near the prep cooler to have dust debris.  Clean the fan as needed.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
